> People say how they hate surveillance tech, but at the end of the day, it pays half of the bills on this website.

HN has surveillance tech?

> Most probably, there is Google Analytics and Facebook pixel on the very site you are building right now.

Nope. I haven't used any of those since 2016. None of the apps I build for iOS have third party analytics, trackers or even ads. I solely rely on a single one time only in app purchase for monetization. Even my OCR app does all its processing locally on the device itself and none of the data leaves the device. I have a mood tracker app which obviously has a lot of intimate, confidential and private data from users - the data stays on their device and if they use iCloud syncing, then to Apple's server (despite all of Apple's flaws, they do seem to be doing much better when it comes to privacy). I have a school timetable app which also has lot of confidential data. Same thing on that app too - everything stays locally on the device or iCloud if user chooses. I DO NOT want user data. I have a site which is a resume builder which users input a lot of confidential data. Even that site never transfers any of the user data and everything is stored locally on the browser. There isn't even any ads or analytics on the site as can be confirmed by sniffing network requests. I had to spend couple extra weeks to get the PDF generation done locally in the browser instead of sending the user data to some server. This took extra time but it was …

quotes.story_title: Tell HN: My Hacker News app (HACK) is sort of broken this afternoon

quotes.text:
I am the developer for HACK, a hacker news app on iOS, iPadOS, MacOS and Android.

As of this afternoon, I received lots of emails reporting a bug in the app where:

1. Tapping on a story was taking to the link for the story instead of the comments. There was no way to access the comments.

2. All stories showed "now" as the time posted instead of the correct time.

3. Threads didn't display the title for the parent post.

This occurred due to Hacker News making some changes to its website's HTML today.

Since the Hacker News API is pretty much useless (it's a read only API and doesn't allow voting, favoriting, commenting etc. Also very hard to work with), my app relies on the website which it parses to get the content. It does the parsing using XPath. Due to the changes in the HTML, the XPath in the app were no longer valid.

I have already submitted an update to Apple and the Play Store for fixing this bug. Hoping to have it approved soon (hopefully sometime tonight/tomorrow).

I am really sorry about the inconvenience to all the users who rely on my app.

The apps are:

https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/hack-for-hacker-news-reader/id1464477788

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.pranapps.hack

Feel free to ask questions. Thanks.

quotes.story_title: Old hackers like to read HN too

quotes.text:
Hello HN!

I am the developer for HACK, a hacker news client that I have been building and maintaining for over 8 years now on iOS, iPadOS, MacOS and Android.

Wanted to share this news as there's been a ton of interest in these features recently.

Now, you can block AI related posts in the app. You can also disable infinite scrolling to prevent you from doomscrolling.

To enable these, go to app's home screen, then go to settings (top right), then scroll all the way to the bottom and enable these settings.

You can see an example of the effectiveness of the AI blocking toggle below. Across 3 pages of the HN front page which would typically load 90 posts (30 posts per page), a total of 32 post titles were blocked:

https://imgur.com/a/QtcHArF

Full list of all titles which were blocked can be seen here:

https://pastebin.com/HWnv3KrF

You can see this list of blocked posts by tapping the menu button, then "See Blocked Posts".

Currently, these features are available on Apple platforms. I am adding them to the Android client at this moment too.

You can try the Apple versions here:

https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/hack-for-hacker-news-yc-reader/id1464477788

Feel free to ask questions.

quotes.story_title: Ask HN: How do you consume HN?

quotes.text:
Hello HN,

3 years ago, I shared the iOS client for my Hacker News app HACK:

https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/hack-for-hacker-news-developer/id1464477788

Since then I have made it MacOS compatible too.

Last few months, I worked on building my first Kotlin app and built the Android version of HACK.

It has all the awesome features - login with your HN account and swipe to vote, favourite, reply. You can submit new posts too.

I believe my app is the only HN client to have:

1. The app also had a built in reader mode as well as text to speech for an article or comment.

2. Push Notifications for replies to your post or comment.

3. Easily access an article via archive.is or archive.org or google cache

4. Built in browser has an ad blocker.

5. All the endpoints of HN.

6. Updated often. I have been updated the iOS version as often as needed to implement customer requests. Same will apply for Android.

There's tons of customizations settings and colours, fonts, font size change etc available in the app.

The Android version is brand new, so any feedback is appreciated.
